messages:
maria: quick note - ran into two unrelated issues while wiring up tool_call with structured_output in async flow. filing here before I forget.

maria: 1) typing/coercion: I declared structured_output as `Union[Article, ErrorDetail]` where Article and ErrorDetail are dataclasses. When the tool returns an error-shaped payload the coercer occasionally constructs Article with missing fields instead of ErrorDetail. no exceptions thrown, but fields like `body` are None which confuses downstream code.

tony: can you paste the dataclass defs and example payload? union coercion should try each variant in order and pick the first that validates.

maria: defs below:

maria: ```py
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Union

@dataclass
class Article:
    id: str
    title: str
    body: str

@dataclass
class ErrorDetail:
    code: int
    message: str

OutputType = Union[Article, ErrorDetail]
```

maria: example tool response (json): `{"code":400,"message":"invalid query"}`. The coercer sometimes returns Article(id='400', title=None, body=None) rather than ErrorDetail. looks like a permissive coercion path coerces ints->str and missing fields become None.

kevin: that is bad. We should make coercion strict by default for dataclasses used in structured_output. Implicit coercions (int->str) are dangerous. Also union logic should prefer exact field matches.

maria: agreed. My workaround was to add `strict_types=True` in my app-level parser but that's a fragile kludge.

tony: noted. We'll file an SDK change: stricter dataclass enforcement + union disambiguation heuristics. Also add a debug flag to emit which variant matched during coercion.

maria: second issue: auth race on async token refresh. Using AsyncClient with oauth integration. On long-lived processes the first request after token expiry sometimes fails with AuthenticationError even though the client starts a refresh in background. Reproduces more under httpx transport and when many concurrent requests trigger refresh at same time.

kevin: are you using a shared AsyncClient instance across tasks? refresh should be singleflight/locked so only one refresh occurs.

maria: yes, shared instance. It looks like two tasks both see token expired, both call _refresh_token, race on writing new token to session. Observed exception stack: `AuthenticationError: 401` in one task, while another successfully refreshes.

tony: we added a naive lock in the sync client a while back but forgot to mirror the singleflight pattern into AsyncClient for httpx/aiohttp. Totally on us. Fix: implement an asyncio.Lock around refresh and make refresh idempotent. Also ensure requests that triggered refresh wait for the lock and then retry once automatically.

maria: sounds good. One follow-up: documented pattern for users with many concurrent calls would help (e.g., use a pool / refresh prefetch). Put that in the async cookbook.

kevin: agree. Also add an integration test that simulates concurrent expiry with a mocked auth endpoint to catch regressions.

maria: thanks. small ask: could we also add an opt-in param on AsyncClient like `refresh_strategy=\"blocking\"|\"background\"` so apps can choose behavior? For some low-latency paths they prefer background refresh even if first few requests fail.

tony: good idea. add it as an API doc note and flag. We'll discuss tradeoffs.

maria: devex-bot: create two tickets?

devex-bot: created issues RW-4234 (strict-dataclass-union-coercion) and RW-4235 (async-token-refresh-singleflight) assigned to @kevin. Links: https://redwood.atlassian.example/browse/RW-4234 , https://redwood.atlassian.example/browse/RW-4235

kevin: I'll pick them up this sprint. For RW-4234 I'll prototype with pydantic/v2 style strict parsing logic but keep dependence-free for dataclass users. For RW-4235 I'll port the sync client's refresh lock into the AsyncClient and add the `refresh_strategy` option plus tests.

maria: awesome. I'll drop reproducible snippets and an integration test in a PR branch. Thanks! :slightly_smiling_face:
